subject: SIG questionnaire - incident notification & timelines (GreenFintech)
messages:
From: Sarah Keenan <sarah.keenan@greenfintech.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: security@greenfintech.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SIG questionnaire - incident notification & timelines

Alex —

Thanks for the quick turn here. We received the SIG export you shared and have a few follow-up clarifications specifically around incident notification timelines and the contact/escalation matrix. A couple of items flagged on our side:

- If we confirm a data exposure event involving customer data, what is Redwood's committed notification window to customers and to GreenFintech? Our requirements: initial notification within 72 hours after confirmation, and a follow-up with evidence/logs within 7 business days. Can Redwood commit to that cadence?
- Who are the primary and secondary POCs for incident triage, legal escalation, and for handing off evidence requests (audit logs, packet captures, S3 object lists)? We need names, roles, and an escalation order.
- Are there jurisdictions or regulatory dependencies that would change the notification timing (e.g., EU GDPR vs US state law)?

I've attached the SIG export and highlighted the two sections we care about (tabs "IR-timelines" and "Evidence-requests"). We also prefer to lock these into the contract annex if we can — are you able to provide a short statement we can reference?

Can you confirm availability for a 30-minute sync this week (Wed/Thu preferred)?

Appreciate it —
Sarah
Security Program Manager
GreenFintech
[Attachment: GreenFintech_SIG_questions.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: alex.martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Keenan <sarah.keenan@greenfintech.com>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire - incident notification & timelines

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps:

- Notification windows: we can commit to an initial notification to customers and affected partners within 72 hours after confirmation of an incident that meets your exposure threshold. We can provide a follow-up packet (logs and forensic timeline) within 7 business days for most incidents; rare cases requiring extended forensic work may need an agreed extension and we will communicate that.

- POC / escalation: see the attached IR contact matrix (CSV) for names and phone+pager. Summary: primary triage is the on-call incident responder (SoS team) -> Security lead Soojin Lee -> Head of Security (Evelyn Hart) -> Legal (Marissa Cole) for regulatory escalations.

- Jurisdictional differences: our playbook includes jurisdiction-specific notification guidance; for EU GDPR incidents we follow a 72-hour notification-to-authority expectation where applicable. We will surface any cross-border constraints in the incident summary.

Attached: Redwood_Incident_Playbook_v1.3.pdf (section 4 covers timelines), IR_contact_matrix.csv.

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync Wed Aug 12 at 10:00 AM PT to walk through the matrix and the language you can reference in the contract annex. Does that work for you? If you need a faster written statement for procurement, we can provide a short clause draft by EOD tomorrow.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: Redwood_Incident_Playbook_v1.3.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Sarah Keenan <sarah.keenan@greenfintech.com>
To: alex.martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: security@greenfintech.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire - incident notification & timelines

Alex / team —

Thanks, that is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before the call:

1) The 72-hour window you reference — is that after you "confirm" the incident (i.e., after triage establishes scope), or after you are first made aware of a suspected incident? We need the wording to be precise in the annex.
2) For the 7-business-day follow-up: will that include raw audit logs or a curated forensic packet? GreenFintech's security requires access to:
   - authentication logs for affected user IDs
   - request traces including source IPs and agent strings
   - any persisted object lists (S3 object keys) related to the event
3) Evidence custody: who will maintain chain-of-custody and how will we access the artifacts (secure bucket share, special access request, or third-party escrow)?

If you can draft the suggested annex clause (one paragraph) that explicitly states the confirm-vs-discovery timing and the deliverables in the 7-day packet, that will let our procurement/legal folks move quickly.

I'll take Wed 10:00 AM PT for the sync.

— Sarah

From: soojin.lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Keenan <sarah.keenan@greenfintech.com>, alex.martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire - incident notification & timelines

Sarah —

Thanks for the pointed questions. I'll cover each explicitly and attach a one-paragraph draft you can reference in the contract annex.

1) Timing definition: "confirmation" = the point at which our incident response team has validated that a security event meeting our internal incident criteria occurred and has established initial scope. Our commitment is: initial customer/partner notification within 72 hours of confirmation. We will include a short statement of suspected impact in the initial notification; the full forensic deliverable follows.

2) 7-business-day packet contents (standard deliverable):
   - Authentication logs for affected identities (CSV export)
   - Request traces and flow logs (redacted where required for other customers) with source IPs and timestamps
   - List of persisted objects implicated (S3 key list) and a manifest of any exported artifacts
   - Timeline of events (UTC) and actions taken by Redwood responders

3) Evidence custody & access: chain-of-custody will be maintained by Redwood IR with SHA256 checksums for exported artifacts. Access options: (a) secure, time-limited pre-signed S3 share for downloadable artifacts, (b) direct SFTP transfer to an approved GreenFintech endpoint, or (c) shared access to a read-only forensic bucket for the duration of the investigation. We'll agree on the mechanism during the initial call.

Attached is a short annex draft (one paragraph) and the contact matrix CSV with names/phones. If that looks good I will have Legal (Marissa) review the annex language and we can include it in the MSA as an incident-notice addendum.

Action items:
- Alex to confirm the annex wording and share via DocuSign placeholder if GreenFintech is ready.
- Marissa to review annex for legal language; Evelyn to confirm any jurisdictional modifications.
- Schedule: initial notification within 72 hours of confirmation; 7-business-day packet thereafter unless extended by mutual agreement.

Thanks — talk Wed 10:00 AM PT.

Soojín Lee
Director, Security Operations, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199
